name: Semiconductor Specialty Chemicals
scope: Indian listed companies developing, qualifying or building capacity for the electronic-grade chemicals, gases and materials that India's new fabs and ATMP/OSAT plants need, plus the adjacent fab and packaging builders and the Semicon 2.0 policy behind the demand.

summary.one_line: India's chip plants are now shipping, but 85-90% of the specialty chemicals they use are still imported. Semicon 2.0, notified on 31 Aug 2026, pays 30% of capex for materials, chemicals and gases plants, and global incumbents (Fujifilm, Sumitomo) are moving first. Among listed Indian companies, only Acutaas, Tatva Chintan, Aether and Stallion have reached hard semiconductor milestones, and their share prices have moved well ahead of semiconductor revenue.
key_points: Policy rates are now confirmed. Semicon 2.0 (outlay ₹1,27,500 crore, notified 31 Aug 2026) gives equipment and materials makers 30% capex support plus a 10% production-linked incentive from FY2028-29. Silicon fabs get 40% (down from a flat 50% under ISM 1.0) and compound-semiconductor fabs 35% (S2).

Import dependence is severe. 85-90% of specialty chemicals and more than 90% of equipment used by India's chip plants are imported (S1). India imports nearly 100% of its ultra-pure process chemicals and high-purity HF (S4). Electronic specialty gas imports are estimated at USD 800-1,100 mn in 2026, or 65-70% of that market (S5).

Purity is the barrier, not the chemistry. Industrial grade is about 99.9% pure, while semiconductor grade (9N) is 99.9999999% (S4). Tatva Chintan needed about 8-9 years of R&D before a customer qualified its first commercial batch (S10).

Global incumbents are localising first. Fujifilm will invest about ₹800 crore in a Dholera materials plant from Oct 2026, with production targeted for FY2028 (S21). Sumitomo Chemical signed an MoU on 18 Sep 2026 to supply photoresists and high-purity H2O2, IPA, ammonia water and sulfuric acid to Tata Electronics' USD 11 bn fab, and to explore making them in India (S6).

Acutaas is the most advanced Indian listed company. Its 75%-owned Korean JV Indichem (KRW 30 bn, ~₹200 crore) opened in Gongju in Aug 2026 (S7). Its board also approved ₹212 crore for up to 81,000 tonnes a year of electronic-grade chemicals in Gujarat by FY28 (S22).

Indian companies are entering by three routes: a JV next to customers (Acutaas-J & Materials) (S7), an overseas acquisition (Anupam Rasayan's USD 150 mn Jayhawk deal) (S9), or organic build-out (Tatva, Aether, Navin, Stallion) (S10, S11, S13, S17).

The downstream demand base is now real. Kaynes' Sanand OSAT is targeting ₹250-300 crore of semiconductor revenue in FY27 (S23). CG Semi (CG Power-Renesas) began commercial production on 4 Jul 2026 (S24). Archean's SiCSem and RIR Power are building SiC capacity in Odisha (S19, S25).

Markets have run ahead of revenue. Aether is up 109% in CY2026 (S12), and JM Financial's Acutaas forecasts depend on the Korean ramp-up (S8). Semiconductor sales are still at validation or early commercial stage across the chemical names (S10, S11, S13).

for_investors.title: Who benefits
points: Acutaas: a Korean refining and qualification plant inside the customer ecosystem (S7), plus a Gujarat electronic-grade chemicals plant due by FY28 (S22). JM Financial sees specialty chemicals rising from ₹170 crore to ₹730 crore over FY26-30 (S8).
Tatva Chintan: its first commercial-scale semiconductor chemical has been qualified at the most stringent grade, and five more products are in development (S10).

Gas and packaging suppliers, whose demand depends on plant start-ups rather than new-molecule qualification. Linde India has a Dholera ASU due H2 2027 and Sanand land for a packaging-gas site (S16). Stallion's Khalapur facility has been running since 21 Sep 2026 (S17).
Fab and OSAT builders with scheme support: Kaynes (S23), CG Power via CG Semi (S24), Archean via SiCSem (S18, S19) and RIR Power (S25).

for_investors.title: Who is hurt / risks
points: Global incumbents are localising. Fujifilm (S21) and Sumitomo (S6) aim to make chemicals next to the Tata fab, which could crowd out newer Indian suppliers in the same product lines.
Qualification takes years and can fail. Tatva took 8-9 years to reach its first commercial batch (S10).
Valuations have moved ahead of revenue. Aether is up 109% in CY2026 (S12), while its semiconductor sales are only starting in Q2 FY27 (S11).
Slow ramps: Stallion expects only about 20% utilisation in the first year at Khalapur (S17). Linde's gas projects are front-loaded capex with slow revenue realisation (S16).

for_investors.title: What to watch
points: Aether's first Site 5 semiconductor sales (guided for Q2 FY27, reported in the Q2 results due Oct-Nov 2026) and a dedicated block by Q3 FY27 (S11).
The first approvals under the Semicon 2.0 machines-and-materials pillar that name a listed Indian company (S2).
Acutaas' Indichem customer validation and progress on its ₹212 crore Gujarat plant (S7, S22).
Kaynes' application for a USD 1 bn OSAT expansion under Semicon 2.0 (S23), and RIR Power's start of commercial production once regulatory formalities are complete (S25).
Navin's ₹90 crore advanced-materials capacity (Q2 FY28) (S13) and Linde's Dholera ASU (H2 2027) (S16).

subsections.title: What a fab or ATMP plant needs from chemistry

blocks.text: Why purity is the hard part: industrial-grade chemicals are around 99.9% pure, while semiconductor grade (9N) is 99.9999999% (S4). A supplier must also pass the customer's multi-stage qualification before any volume is sold. At Tatva Chintan this took about 8-9 years of R&D before the first commercial batch (S10). Acutaas's Korean plant exists to do this final refining, testing and qualification next to customers, with impurities measured in parts per billion (S7).

items: 85-90% of specialty chemicals and more than 90% of equipment used by India's chip plants are imported, mainly from Japan, Germany, the US and the Netherlands (S1).
India imports nearly 100% of its ultra-pure process chemicals, neon, krypton, arsine and high-purity hydrogen fluoride (S4).

Electronic specialty gases: IndexBox estimates imports at USD 800-1,100 mn in 2026 (65-70% of market value) and puts the total market at USD 1.2-1.6 bn, with semiconductor fabrication more than 55% of demand (S5).
The brief's figure of more than 70% imported is consistent with these estimates. Estimates vary with scope: about 65-70% for gases (S5) and 85-90% for specialty chemicals (S1).

blocks.text: ISM 1.0 was notified in Dec 2021 with a ₹76,000 crore outlay and a flat 50% subsidy (S2). Twelve chip sites have been approved, and assembly operations such as Micron, Kaynes and CG Semi are now shipping (S1, S23, S24). Semicon 2.0 (₹1,27,500 crore) was notified on 31 Aug 2026 with six pillars: design, equipment and materials, fabs, ATMP/OSAT, research and talent (S2). Last week's edition flagged that the materials incentive rate was unconfirmed. ThePrint's reading of the notified scheme now confirms 30% capex support plus a 10% production-linked incentive from FY2028-29 for equipment and materials makers. Silicon fabs get 40%, compound-semiconductor/display/specialised fabs 35%, and projects above ₹500 crore need Cabinet approval, with a three-year application window (S2).

subsections.title: Capex and scheme support by named companies

items: Fujifilm (not listed in India): about ₹800 crore (USD 83 mn) greenfield materials plant in Dholera in two phases, first front-end materials and then surface-conditioning materials and high-purity chemicals. Investment starts Oct 2026, production is targeted for FY2028, and it aims to use Semicon 2.0 support (S21).

Acutaas: board approved ₹212 crore on 22 Aug 2026 for up to 81,000 tonnes a year of electronic-grade chemicals in Gujarat by 31 Mar 2028, funded from internal accruals and bank debt (S22). This comes on top of KRW 30 bn in Indichem Korea (S7).

SiCSem (Archean): signed an ISM fiscal-support agreement on 11 May 2026 at a project cost of about ₹2,066.7 crore (S18). Odisha cleared the unit at ₹3,406 crore on 15-16 Sep 2026, with ₹700 crore of central and ₹350 crore of state support reported (S19). The two cost figures differ and are shown as reported.
Kaynes: plans to apply under Semicon 2.0 for a USD 1 bn OSAT expansion in Gujarat, on top of its ₹3,307 crore Sanand plant (S23).
CG Semi (CG Power-Renesas-Stars JV): more than ₹7,600 crore over five years for the G1 and G2 OSAT plants (S24).
RIR Power: a ₹618 crore SiC plant in Bhubaneswar under Odisha's semiconductor policy (S25).
No listed chemical maker in this universe has yet publicly confirmed an approval under the Semicon 2.0 materials pillar.

blocks.text: Corrections to last week's edition. Aether's semiconductor products are low-dielectric monomers, which management calls advanced electronic materials rather than fab consumables, and first Site 5 sales are guided for Q2 FY27 (S11). Stallion's Khalapur line is a high-purity liquid-helium and specialty-gas line, not the CF4/SF6 blending described earlier (S17).

subsections.title: Gases, fabs, OSAT and adjacent infrastructure

items: Linde India (LINDEINDIA): on 28 Sep 2026 it secured about 8 acres in Sanand for a high-purity chip-packaging gas facility aimed at Micron, CG Power and Kaynes. Its Dholera ASU is due H2 2027 to supply the Tata fab (S16).

Stallion (STALLION): its 1,200 tonnes-per-year Khalapur facility (high-purity liquid-helium processing and a specialty-gas line) started commercial operations on 21 Sep 2026. Management expects about 20% utilisation in the first year (S17).
Kaynes Technology (KAYNES): its Sanand OSAT plant is commercial. It is targeting ₹250-300 crore of semiconductor revenue in FY27, with about ₹100 crore booked (S23).
CG Power (CGPOWER): its JV CG Semi (with Renesas and Stars Microelectronics) started commercial production at the G1 OSAT on 4 Jul 2026, with peak capacity of 300 mn units a year (S24).
Archean (ACI): its subsidiary SiCSem is building a SiC fab plus ATMP with Clas-SiC (UK), cleared by Odisha for 4.8 mn diodes and 91.2 mn MOSFETs a year (S3, S19).
RIR Power Electronics (BSE 517035): completed installation of SiC epitaxial-wafer reactors in Bhubaneswar on 16 Sep 2026. Commercial production awaits the remaining regulatory formalities (S25).

blocks.text: Market-cap coverage: the universe runs from large caps (SRF, Linde India, Navin, GFL) to small caps (Tatva, Stallion, Archean, RIR Power). No other small-cap Indian chemical maker with a cited, semiconductor-grade programme turned up this week. The niche is genuinely thin, so none were added just to fill a size tier.

blocks.text: What the market is pricing in: the re-rating has come at the qualification stage, before any meaningful semiconductor revenue has been disclosed. JM Financial's Acutaas forecasts depend on the Korean ramp-up (S8), and Aether's first Site 5 semiconductor sales are only now starting (S11). Current multiples and distance from 52-week highs come from the dashboard's screener data and are not repeated here.

items: JM Financial on Acutaas (10 Sep 2026): upgraded from Add to Buy. It forecasts specialty chemicals rising from ₹170 crore in FY26 to ₹730 crore in FY30 (45% CAGR), driven by electrolyte additives and semiconductor chemicals, conditional on the Korean ramp-up (S8).
ICICI Securities on Tatva Chintan (20 Jul 2026): issued a price objective after Q1 FY27, when profit rose 140% to ₹16 crore and revenue rose 43% to ₹167.1 crore (S10).

Coverage skew: the named broker actions found were positive, but coverage of the semiconductor angle is thin. Brokers treat it as optionality within wider CDMO or specialty-chemicals stories rather than modelling it as a separate segment (S8, S10). No named broker view specific to the semiconductor angle was found for the gas, fab or OSAT names this week.

blocks.text: This report does not issue ratings or price targets. Broker views are attributed and shown for context only.

items: Qualification timelines: Tatva took about 8-9 years to reach a first commercial batch (S10). Customer audits can reset the clock.
Incumbent localisation: Fujifilm (₹800 crore, Dholera) and Sumitomo are setting up next to the Tata fab (S21, S6). Linde is building local gas capacity (S16).

Demand timing: the Tata Dholera fab is expected to start commercial production only in mid-2028 (S1). Until then, domestic demand comes mainly from OSAT units, which use far less chemistry than front-end fabs.
Utilisation and gestation: Stallion guides about 20% first-year utilisation (S17). Linde flags multi-year gestation for semiconductor gas revenue (S16).
Conflicting project data: SiCSem is reported at both ₹2,066.7 crore (S18) and ₹3,406 crore (S19).

items: Watch each quarter: disclosed semiconductor revenue or volumes, new customer qualifications, capex spend against plan, Semicon 2.0 approvals naming listed companies, and new JV or technology tie-ups with Japanese, Korean or US suppliers.

companies.name: Acutaas Chemicals
companies.role: Makes ultra-high-purity semiconductor materials. Synthesis is done in India; refining and qualification happen at the Indichem Inc. plant in Gongju, Korea (75% owned; J & Materials holds 25%; KRW 30 bn invested), opened Aug 2026 (S7). Its board also approved ₹212 crore for an electronic-grade chemicals plant in Gujarat (up to 81,000 tonnes a year, by FY28) (S22).
companies.impact: The most advanced qualification route in the universe, now with two semiconductor capex legs. JM Financial expects specialty chemicals to reach ₹730 crore by FY30, contingent on the Korean ramp-up (S8). Fujifilm and Sumitomo plans in Dholera are direct competition for wet chemicals (S21, S6).

companies.name: Tatva Chintan Pharma Chem
companies.role: Delivered and qualified its first commercial-scale semiconductor chemical (a key starting raw material, most stringent grade) in Q1 FY27, after about 8-9 years of R&D. Five more products are in development (S10).
companies.impact: A first-mover with qualification proven. The stock hit a 20% upper circuit on 20 Jul 2026 (S10). The segment is still small against ₹167 crore of quarterly revenue (S10).

companies.name: Aether Industries
companies.role: Developing low-dielectric monomers for 5G and AI hardware. Qualification batches have been made at Site 3, and first commercial sales from Site 5 are guided for Q2 FY27 (S11).
companies.impact: A dedicated semiconductor block is due by Q3 FY27 (S11). The stock is up 109% in CY2026 (S12). These are advanced electronic materials rather than fab consumables, so they are less tied to India's fab timeline (S11).

companies.name: Anupam Rasayan India
companies.role: Acquired US-based Jayhawk Fine Chemicals for USD 150 mn (closed 28 Feb 2026), which brings molecules for electronics and semiconductors (S9).
companies.impact: Took the acquisition route: it bought existing US manufacturing and customer qualifications instead of building them. The risks are integration and acquisition funding (S9).

companies.name: Navin Fluorine International
companies.role: Building a ₹90 crore advanced-materials adoption capacity at Surat (due Q2 FY28) for data-centre, electronics and semiconductor uses. Electronic-grade HF is named as a future component (S13).
companies.impact: HF integration gives it a natural route into etchants, but the business is still an incubation vertical meant to become material by the end of the decade (S13).

companies.name: Gujarat Fluorochemicals
companies.role: Incorporated GFCL Semiconductor and Advanced Materials Ltd on 26 Jun 2026 with ₹1 lakh of initial capital (S15).
companies.impact: Early optionality only. No product, capex or partner has been disclosed for the new subsidiary (S15).

companies.name: SRF
companies.role: Signed supply and production agreements with Chemours (Aug 2025) covering fluoropolymers and specialty fluorochemicals used in semiconductor manufacturing and electronics (S14).
companies.impact: Semiconductor exposure is indirect, through fluoropolymers, and is not disclosed separately (S14).

companies.name: Tata Chemicals
companies.role: Markets dense soda ash and nano zinc oxide to electronics and semiconductor manufacturing, but does not describe them as semiconductor-grade (S20).
companies.impact: No disclosed semiconductor-chemical programme. The link is its group: Tata Electronics' MoU with Sumitomo Chemical for photoresists and high-purity chemicals does not involve Tata Chemicals (S6).

companies.name: Linde India
companies.role: Building an air separation unit at Dholera, due H2 2027, to supply the Tata fab. On 28 Sep 2026 it secured about 8 acres in Sanand for a high-purity chip-packaging gas facility (S16).
companies.impact: A direct beneficiary of plant start-ups (Micron, CG Power, Kaynes in Sanand), with revenue tied to plant start-ups rather than qualification risk. Revenue will build gradually after front-loaded capex (S16).

companies.name: Stallion India Fluorochemicals
companies.role: Runs a 1,200 tonnes-per-year facility at Khalapur, Maharashtra for high-purity liquid-helium processing and specialty semiconductor/electronics gases. Commercial operations started on 21 Sep 2026 (S17).
companies.impact: The only listed Indian company in this universe with dedicated semiconductor-gas handling capacity in operation. Guided utilisation is about 20% in year one (S17).

companies.name: Archean Chemical Industries
companies.role: Its subsidiary SiCSem is building a SiC compound-semiconductor fab plus ATMP in Odisha with Clas-SiC (UK), under an ISM fiscal-support agreement signed 11 May 2026 (S3, S18).
companies.impact: A direct ISM beneficiary. Project cost is reported at ₹2,066.7 crore (S18) and ₹3,406 crore, with ₹700 crore of central and ₹350 crore of state support (S19). It is a large bet relative to the core bromine and salt business.

companies.name: Kaynes Technology India
companies.role: Runs a ₹3,307 crore OSAT plant at Sanand under ISM 1.0 that is now commercial (S23).
companies.impact: Targets ₹250-300 crore of semiconductor revenue in FY27, with about ₹100 crore booked, and plans a USD 1 bn Semicon 2.0 expansion (S23). It is a demand anchor for Sanand's gases and chemicals (S16).

companies.name: CG Power and Industrial Solutions
companies.role: Its JV CG Semi (with Renesas and Stars Microelectronics) began commercial production at the G1 OSAT in Sanand on 4 Jul 2026, with peak capacity of 300 mn units a year (S24).
companies.impact: More than ₹7,600 crore is planned over five years for the G1 and G2 plants (S24). It is a named prospective customer for Linde's Sanand gas site (S16).

companies.name: RIR Power Electronics
companies.role: Completed installation of SiC epitaxial-wafer reactors at its ₹618 crore Bhubaneswar facility on 16 Sep 2026. It plans SiC MOSFETs, diodes and modules (S25).
companies.impact: A small-cap compound-semiconductor entrant, with commercial production pending regulatory formalities (S25). It overlaps with SiCSem in Odisha's SiC cluster (S19).

method: W40 refresh on 29 Sep 2026, re-verifying last week's edition with web search and direct page fetches. Changes this week: Semicon 2.0 notified rates (via ThePrint) replace the earlier unconfirmed 30% figure. Added Fujifilm's Dholera plan, Acutaas' ₹212 crore electronic-grade capex, Linde's Sanand land (28 Sep) and RIR Power's SiC reactors. Added OSAT builders Kaynes and CG Power and small-cap RIR Power. Corrected the Aether product description and the Stallion gas mix. Dropped items that could not be re-confirmed this week: the Buss ChemTech HF tie-up detail, Jayhawk deal-structure details, the SRF capex figure, the Acutaas one-year return and the Indichem FY28 revenue guidance. Some pages (Business Standard, gasworld, Digitimes, YourStory) blocked direct fetch; for these, only facts shown in search-result snippets are used, marked 'search-result summary'. Where a publication date could not be confirmed, the access date is shown. Where sources conflict (SiCSem project cost; import-share scope), both figures are shown. Broker views are attributed by name. This report issues no ratings or price targets. Valuation multiples come from the dashboard's screener data.
